title: DaVinci Resolve Studio 21 US$236 / A$360 (Was US$295), & 20% off Editing Keyboards / Color Panels @ Black Magic Design
body:
Deal: DaVinci Resolve Studio 21 US$236 / A$360 (Was US$295), & 20% off Editing Keyboards / Color Panels @ Black Magic Design

[wisc] I use the free version for the odd family video once ever years or so, it's pretty powerful. I can only imagine how good the paid version would be…
[Jake T] It’s not necessarily “better”, but the features make it more suitable for people working in the field. Both versions are great for their intended audience 👌
[LuvzABargain] I'm waiting for the free full feature Artcraft version.
[KaliKaliKali] Blackmagic has been one of the good guys for a consistently long time. Local Melbourne company. Always done good by their customers. Worth supporting them.
Quote from their CEO Grant Petty:
"You have no idea how many MBA-type thinkers have told me we have to charge a monthly fee for DaVinci Resolve… or have told me to think of massive profits instead of helping solve our customer's problems. Blackmagic does not look at our customers as targets to squeeze as much money as possible out of."
[Kawaii] Does the editing keyboard gives free activation of studio software ?
[prsam1] Been using this for a few years now and have been really happy with it - and paid much more than this at the time! Also nice to support an Australian company
[ngengerous] Making the switch from Premiere to Resolve a few years back did come with a bit of a learning curve - but I have never looked back. If you're still subscribed to Adobe for Premiere/After Effects, I'd really strongly consider swapping over now. You'll save a ton of cash and get a fantastic product.
[Nerdybobo] FFS… I brought my license about a week ago.. <sigh>
[Nerdybobo] Btw just from a Linux users prospective, it works pretty well. You probably don't need the payed version for the most part but these guys have done a great job in developing it and making it available on Linux, I think that alone just makes them worth the investment. It doesn't support AAC audio which is pretty much used everywhere but that's a licencing issue I believe not a limitation in the software on Linux. There is work around. And the video codecs as well is limited with the free version on Cachyos. You can get around it of you convert your videos first but it's a time and storage situation then. Long sorry short it's been good so far in the week that I've had it and no real regrets except not waiting to see this on ozbargins! I guess supporting these guys for making this product is worth it still :)
[wishing well] Studio is $375 for me. Still great value.
